name: Garratt Road Bridge
facts: Garratt Road Bridge, the longest timber bridge still standing in Western Australia, stretches 238 metres across the Swan River, its 38 timber spans originally erected in 1935 to ferry two lanes of traffic and pedestrians.

The downstream twin, completed in 1972, was designed with only a 40‑year lifespan, anticipating redundancy once Tonkin Highway opened, yet Main Roads retrofitted steel girders and concrete overlays to extend its life beyond expectations.

Heritage recognition followed decades of service: first listed in the City of Bayswater’s Municipal Heritage Inventory in 1998, then added to the state heritage list in 2009, cementing its cultural and engineering significance.
